newsitem.title: USA: Phillips sees steady exploration spending.
newsitem.headline: Phillips sees steady exploration spending.

text.p: Phillips Petroleum Co plans to hold exploration spending worldwide steady at $300 million a year for the next few years, Chairman Wayne Allen said on Thursday.
The Bartlesville, Okla.-based oil company earmarked one third of its exploration budget for "new" exploration prospects in the Gulf of Mexico and overseas, he said.
"We have a saying at Phillips, what is it -- budget interruptis -- they are not going to have it in exploration," Allen said in a meeting with reporters in Houston.
Allen said a squeeze in rigs available for offshore drilling in the Gulf of Mexico was increasing pressure on producers to ink long-term contracts, which producers have largely resisted.

But he said the industry's pace of deepwater drilling will continue to accelerate despite the risks of moving into a largely unexplored area. "It's getting tougher to replace that domestic barrel," he said.

Phillips on Wednesday reported third quarter net income of $187 million or $0.71 a share, a 38 percent increase over $136 million or $0.52 a share in the same period last year. Revenues rose to $3.9 billion versus $3.4 billion a year ago.
